model_interpretation.claim: The selected 4x1 parent keeps a 32x32 CTA output tile and measured 0.014726 s; the measured 2x4 mapping was faster at 0.011853 s, while a 1x4 mapping measured 0.037572 s. Those outcomes do not isolate the mapping effect. This experiment keeps the parent's 32x32 output tile but maps 128 threads to 4x2 microtiles (eight FP32 accumulators each), reusing each A value across two columns and each B value across four rows. It tests whether that orientation improves operand reuse without the same lane mapping as 2x4; register pressure, coalescing, or fewer threads may instead hurt. Correctness, repeated timing, and register/occupancy results are still needed, including comparison with the one-output-per-thread control.

model_interpretation.claim: A 2x2 output microtile gives each thread four independent FP32 accumulators while reusing each loaded A value across two columns and each B value across two rows. Keeping a 32x32 CTA output tile and 256 threads makes this a mapping comparison with the measured four-row parent rather than a larger CTA-work comparison.
